value.rationale: Number variance is used as a scale-dependent pseudo-randomness diagnostic, yet separate marginal calibrations do not quantify dependence of simultaneous windows. The exact all-N cross-length covariance and stationary log-scale Gaussian kernel provide a natural multiscale calibration object, distinguish nearby from well-separated scales, and exhibit a non-rank-one universal dependence law. This is not simply a single-length variance substitution; it resolves the joint law needed for finite multi-scale inference, without claiming a full process theorem.
